question: Should OpenClaw make model-authored `<details>/<summary>` a supported cross-channel response feature, with native rendering limited to the Control UI and Telegram rich mode and portable flattening elsewhere?
rationale: The patch is not only a parser repair: it establishes user-visible semantics for model-produced HTML across transports, which needs explicit maintainer acceptance before becoming a durable product contract.

options.title: Approve the scoped disclosure contract
options.body: Accept native Control UI and Telegram rich rendering plus portable flattening for other channels after real behavior proof is added.

options.title: Narrow the feature surface
options.body: Keep the renderer change limited to the Control UI until channel-specific disclosure behavior has a separately agreed contract.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause the PR if model-authored HTML disclosures are not a desired supported response format.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped disclosure contract
recommendation.body: Accept native Control UI and Telegram rich rendering plus portable flattening for other channels after real behavior proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to steipete and the available branch history shows steipete authored the implementation under review.
